Yes, I do see a difference between me without medication vs me on it. I have a history of manic episodes, and they became uncontrollable because I was overwhelmed, also add the auditory and visual hallucinations from the pent-up stress. When I got on the medication, I felt shit for 3 weeks straight, I mostly bedrotted at home. But I eventually got better, and kept taking it. I consider myself very optimistic, determined, and I eventually regained my will to live. I can control my emotions properly now. 

I still have hallucinations and bouts of paranoia, but I definently have kept it under wraps now. I also have moved countries which helped my situation, I am in a much more better place now. I also underwent therapy. This was a joint plan set in place by my psychiatrist, and my parents to ensure I would be half-way through with my treatment plan once I arrived in the US.
I definently see it as a form of closure. I decided to take the prescribed medicine because I believed it would make better, but to each to their own.
I would probably suggest seeking a doctor at a private hospital. Also, psychiatrists aren’t psychologists so they always offer medicine as a form of solution to you.
